signals.entity: All SEPA-scheme PSPs (AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK euro-area; CZ, HU, RO non-euro EU; plus SEPA-geography RS, ME, AL, MK)
signals.signal: EPC Guidance EPC153-22 v2.1 (issued and effective 05/10/2025), verified against the primary PDF this run, fixes 15/11/2026 - and 03h30 CET for the SCT Inst and OCT Inst schemes - as the date from which ONLY structured and hybrid addresses are allowed, both Inter-PSP and in Customer-to-PSP ISO 20022 XML files: 'The use of an unstructured address will no longer be allowed and will hence lead to rejects.' Section 6.4 records the underlying SWIFT decision of December 2023: hybrid address introduced by November 2025 WITH NO EXPIRATION DATE, unstructured allowed only until November 2026. The 15/11 date (moved from 22/11/2026) was aligned to the SWIFT Standards MX Release in the second full weekend of November 2026.
signals.source_name: European Payments Council, EPC153-22 v2.1 'Provision of Addresses under the EPC Payment Schemes' (PDF)
signals.implies: Hard reject risk on 15/11/2026 for every footprint PSP still holding free-text addresses. The remediation is customer-data cleansing plus sanctions/AML screening re-tuning on the new structured fields (IMTF Siron, FICO), onboarding capture of town+country as discrete fields (Namirial eKYC), and reject/NAK monitoring at cutover (INETCO). Confirms hybrid is a permanent landing zone, so banks do NOT need full structuring - a materially cheaper scope than most vendors are selling.
signals.followup: Budget-commit window for this date (6-12 months prior) has CLOSED. Sell remediation/managed-services and reject-handling, not programme work. Pitch hybrid-only scope to cap cost.

signals.entity: SWIFT CBPR+ users - all footprint banks with correspondent flows
signals.country: Footprint-wide (incl. non-EU: RS, BA, ME, MK, AL, XK, UA)
signals.signal: SWIFT Standards Release SR2026 removes unstructured postal addresses from CBPR+ on 14/11/2026; messages carrying them are rejected (NAK'ed) at network level. Corroborated at primary level by EPC153-22 v2.1 s6.4, which records SWIFT's December 2023 decision to allow unstructured only until November 2026 and aligns the EPC end date to 'the November 2026 Swift Standards MX Release scheduled in the second full weekend of November 2026' (= 14-15/11/2026). Swift.com's own pages (removal-unstructured-address, call-action-november-2026, the SR2026 news item and the AI address-structuring model page) were NOT openable from this environment - see access_issues - so the network-level NAK mechanic and the camt/admi exemption list are corroborated only from search-result extracts of those pages, not from a page I opened.
signals.source_name: EPC153-22 v2.1 s6.4 (primary corroboration of the SWIFT date); underlying SWIFT page not openable
signals.implies: Non-EU footprint banks (Serbia, BiH, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo, Ukraine) have NO domestic scheme forcing this, but their correspondent-banking flows die on 14/11/2026 regardless. That is the single largest un-owned remediation pocket in the footprint. Maps to AML/KYC data remediation (Siron/FICO), eKYC address capture (Namirial) and managed services.
signals.followup: Operator to fetch the swift.com SR2026 pages and the CBPR+ 'Community Requirements Info sheet' (swift.com/swift-resource/252559/download) to confirm the exempted message identifiers.

signals.entity: T2 (TARGET Services) - all direct participants incl. AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK banks
signals.country: Euro area (AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK)
signals.signal: Deutsche Bundesbank release briefing 'Information on T2 R2026.NOV Release' (30/04/2026) sets the full window: release testing in UTEST/Pre-Production opens 25/09/2026 and CLOSES 28/10/2026; deployment in production 14/11/2026 (first business day 16/11/2026). Four change requests carry functional implications for market participants: T2-0135-SYS (additional CRDM routing configurations for network-service-provider failure scenarios), T2-0147-SYS (upgrade of T2 messages to ISO MR 2025), T2-0156-UDFS (HVPS Plus UG2026 maintenance on T2 RTGS messages) and T2-0170-SYS.
signals.source_name: Deutsche Bundesbank, 'TARGET Service T2 - Information on T2 R2026.NOV Release' (PDF, 30/04/2026)
signals.implies: The 28/10/2026 end-of-testing date is the real hard stop for footprint banks, not 16/11 - any fix not proven in UTEST by 28/10 goes live untested. T2-0135-SYS (NSP failure routing) is a resilience change that touches connectivity configuration and is a managed-services / operational-readiness engagement.
signals.followup: Confirm which footprint banks are direct vs indirect T2 participants; indirect participants inherit the deadline via their correspondent.

signals.country: Euro area (AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK)
signals.signal: MATERIAL SCOPE CORRECTION. ECB change request T2-0170-SYS (raised September 2025, status Approved, published 17/10/2025) states explicitly: 'Seven core payment messages (pacs.002, pacs.004, pacs.008, pacs.009, pacs.010, camt.029 and camt.056) in T2 RTGS shall remain on ISO MR2019 in November 2026 and will be probably migrated to ISO MR2025 in November 2027.' T2 messages move to ISO MR2024 in T2 R2026.JUN and to MR2025/MR2026 for the non-core set; the November 2026 upgrade for RTGS touches only camt.053, camt.054 (RTGS+CLM) and CLM-only messages.
signals.source_name: ECB / 4CB, 'T2-0170-SYS Upgrade of T2 Messages to ISO MR 2026' change request form
signals.implies: The November 2026 address break for euro-area banks does NOT come from T2 RTGS schema versions - it comes from CBPR+ (14/11) and the EPC schemes (15/11), plus HVPS+ UG2026 usage guidelines. Any vendor pitching a 'T2 pacs.008 schema migration' for Nov-2026 is mis-scoping. The genuine T2 RTGS schema wave is November 2027 - that is where the forward budget-commit window sits (commit Nov-2026 to May-2027).
signals.followup: Track T2-0156-UDFS (HVPS Plus UG2026) for the actual RTGS address usage rules; confirm the Nov-2027 MR2025 migration is formally scheduled.

signals.entity: BNB / TARGET-BNB and 19 named Bulgarian banks + BORICA AD
signals.signal: Following euro adoption, the BNB's national TARGET component TARGET-BNB is live with updated operating rules IN FORCE FROM 15/06/2026 (plus contingency-processing measures in force from 01/01/2026). BNB publishes the participant list: Allianz Bank Bulgaria, DSK Bank, Bulgarian-American Credit Bank, Bulgarian Development Bank, BNB, Investbank, International Asset Bank, UBB, Municipal Bank, ProCredit Bank Bulgaria, First Investment Bank, T.C. Ziraat Bankasi Sofia branch, Texim Bank, TBI Bank, Tokuda Bank, D Commerce Bank, UniCredit Bulbank, Central Cooperative Bank, Eurobank Bulgaria - plus ancillary systems BISERA and BORICA, both operated by BORICA AD.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank, 'Platezhna sistema T2' / TARGET-BNB participants and legal framework page
signals.implies: Bulgaria moved from national-currency RINGS to full T2 participation inside one year. All 19 named banks are now inside the T2 R2026.NOV testing window (UTEST 25/09-28/10/2026) and inside the EPC 15/11/2026 address regime, with no legacy grace. BORICA AD as operator of both ancillary systems is a single high-leverage integration counterparty. Maps to AML screening re-tuning (Siron/FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO) and managed services during a compressed dual change.
signals.followup: Confirm which of the 19 are direct T2 participants; approach BORICA AD as scheme-level integrator. Reconcile with the contested 01/01/2027 BG instant/VoP legal basis carried as a verification debt.

signals.entity: CBBH (Central Bank of Bosnia & Herzegovina) - RTGS
signals.signal: CBBH Governing Board decision of 20/12/2025 (ref UV-122-02-1-1903-4/25), published in Sluzbeni glasnik BiH No. 09/26 of 06/02/2026 ['Official Gazette of BiH'], amends Art.12 of the RTGS operating rules: 'Do dana prelaska na upotrebu novog SWIFT MX formata poruka, vrste poruka placanja su: MT102, MT103, MT202 i MT205' [Until the day of the switch to the new SWIFT MX message format, the payment message types are MT102, MT103, MT202 and MT205], with mandatory header field 103 service code BAP; and 'Upotreba MX formata poruka i koristenje poruka placanja: pacs.008 i pacs.009 zapocet ce po zavrsetku tehnicke i operativne pripreme svih ucesnika i uskladjivanja sa standardom ISO 20022. Guverner Centralne banke ce odrediti tacan datum... najmanje 15 dana prije istog' [Use of MX and pacs.008/pacs.009 will begin once all participants complete technical and operational preparation and ISO 20022 alignment; the Governor will set the exact date and notify participants in writing at least 15 days beforehand].
signals.source_name: Sluzbeni glasnik BiH br. 09/26, 06/02/2026 - Odluka o izmjeni i dopunama Odluke o utvrdjivanju operativnih pravila za bruto poravnanje u realnom vremenu (CBBH, Governor Jasmina Selimovic)
signals.implies: BiH high-value RTGS is legally pinned to SWIFT MT with NO published MX date and only 15 days' statutory notice - the shortest lead time to a live ISO 20022 cutover anywhere in the footprint. Affected: Raiffeisen BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, UniCredit Bank d.d./a.d., Sparkasse Bank, NLB Banka, Addiko, ASA Banka, ProCredit and the rest of the RTGS participant set. Because the Governor's trigger is 'all participants ready', every laggard bank is on the critical path - a classic readiness-assessment plus message-transformation and monitoring engagement (INETCO for pacs.008 decoding; Siron/FICO for structured-address screening).
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that a Governor's notice is issued within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Monitor CBBH Javni registar propisa and Sluzbeni glasnik BiH for the Governor's notice; 15 days is not enough lead time to start selling, so position now.

signals.entity: CBBH Ziro kliring (BiH retail clearing) and its participant banks
signals.signal: CBBH states the Ziro kliring system - in production since 03/06/2019 for interbank credit transfers up to BAM 10,000 in four daily cycles - uses SEPA-format messages compliant with ISO 20022 and the EPC Rulebook version designated as current by the Central Bank: 'Poruke i formati koji se koriste u ovome platnome sustavu su u potpunosti uskladjeni sa porukama i formatima koji se koriste u SEPA podrucju' [The messages and formats used in this payment system are fully aligned with those used in the SEPA area]. A further amending decision (Governing Board 20/12/2025, Gazette 09/26 of 06/02/2026) was adopted alongside the RTGS one, adding Governor discretion over non-working days.
signals.source_name: CBBH, 'Ziro kliring' system page and CBBH press release 'Uskladjivanje platnih sustava sa standardima EU' (06/06/2019); amending decision Gazette 09/26 (06/02/2026)
signals.implies: Contrary to the RTGS position, BiH retail clearing is already ISO 20022 and contractually tethered to whichever EPC rulebook version CBBH designates - so the EPC 15/11/2026 unstructured-address end date can reach BiH banks through Ziro kliring the moment CBBH designates the 2025 rulebook. This is the near-term BiH trigger, and it is not publicly dated. Note the asymmetry to sell against: BiH banks must be structured-address-ready for retail clearing while still sending MT on RTGS.
signals.followup: Ask CBBH which EPC rulebook version is currently designated for Ziro kliring; this determines whether 15/11/2026 binds BiH retail.

signals.entity: MNB VIBER and the nine Hungarian PSPs
signals.signal: VIBER (Hungary's RTGS) completed its MX/ISO 20022 cutover on 27/10/2025 - MNB Business Terms Annex 2 'Benyujtasi rend' effective 27/10/2025 references customer items as 'pacs.008 tipusu SWIFT uzenet' and pacs.009 for participant-initiated orders. HOWEVER, the currently effective MNB annex set (latest annexes dated 03/08/2026) contains NO structured- or hybrid-postal-address rule, and the MNB VIBER page carries no ISO 20022 or November 2026 content. As at 27/08/2026 no MNB publication sets a VIBER hybrid-address date. Hungarian banks are meanwhile telling corporates the SWIFT rule bites: K&H Bank's ISO 20022 customer communication states 'Strukturalatlan cimadatok hasznalata 2026 novemberetol mar nem lesznek megengedett' [Use of unstructured address data will no longer be permitted from November 2026].
signals.source_name: MNB, 'Jelenleg hatalyos Uzleti feltetelek es mellekletei' (annex index, annexes to 03/08/2026) and Annex 2 'Benyujtasi rend' (27/10/2025); K&H Bank 'SWIFT ISO20022 ugyfelkommunikacio'
signals.implies: CONFIRMS AND SHARPENS the baseline VIBER hybrid-address gap: the gap is real and still open 11 weeks before the SEPA/CBPR+ break. Hungarian PSPs (OTP, MBH, Erste Hungary, K&H, CIB, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, Granit, MagNet) must be structured/hybrid-ready for SWIFT and SEPA on 14-15/11/2026 while their domestic RTGS gives them no rule and no date - i.e. they will run two address regimes. Sell dual-format handling and reject monitoring (INETCO), plus screening re-tune (Siron/FICO).
signals.likelihood: High that Hungarian banks run split address regimes through the Nov-2026 cutover
signals.followup: Watch mnb.hu Uzleti feltetelek for a new annex before 15/11/2026. If none appears, the gap is confirmed operationally.

signals.entity: Croatian SEPA Forum / HNB, FINA EuroNKS and Croatian PSPs
signals.signal: The Croatian SEPA Forum (national SEPA coordination body) published SEPA Newsletter No.18 (December 2025) on the change of the unstructured-address application date, and its site carries the standing banner 'Prestanak koristenja nestrukturirane adrese od 15. studenoga 2026. godine' [End of use of the unstructured address from 15 November 2026]. National guidance is that instructions with an execution date from 15/11/2026 will be REJECTED if the payer/payee/PSP address is completed in unstructured form. Croatian client-side guidance already moved to the pain.001 format effective 05/10/2025 (SCTInst client instruction, sepa.hr).
signals.source_name: Croatian SEPA Forum (sepa.hr), 'Novosti' and SEPA Newsletter br.18, Prosinac 2025
signals.implies: Croatia has a functioning national communication channel and an explicit reject warning - so Croatian banks (Zagrebacka/UniCredit, PBZ/Intesa, Erste Croatia, OTP Croatia, RBA Croatia, HPB, Addiko) will have local reject volumes visible at cutover. Erste Croatia is an existing Printec OptiCash customer - a warm route into cutover-period reject handling and screening re-tune.
signals.followup: Obtain SEPA Newsletter br.18 PDF and check for a Croatian-specific reject-handling protocol; check FINA EuroNKS participant guidance.

signals.entity: NBU SEP-4 / SEP-4.1 and Ukrainian banks
signals.signal: NBU primary page confirms Ukraine's SEP (System of Electronic Payments, the national RTGS carrying >99% of interbank payments) has run on ISO 20022 since the SEP-4 go-live on 01/04/2023 and moved to 24/7 operation; SEP-4.1 with instant credit transfer functionality (10-second settlement) has been live since 01/12/2024. SEP averages ~1.5m payments/day worth ~UAH 778bn. Domestic UAH messaging therefore already carries structured ISO 20022 data and is NOT exposed to the November 2026 address break.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine, 'Systema elektronnykh platezhiv' (SEP) official page
signals.implies: Ukraine's ISO 20022 exposure is entirely on the CBPR+ side: PrivatBank (an existing Printec NCR recycler customer), Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Ukraine, UkrSibbank, Ukrgasbank et al must structure the postal-address data in their correspondent-banking messages by 14/11/2026 or lose cross-border settlement. Because there is no domestic driver, this work is easy to under-budget - a genuine late-cycle remediation opening (customer-data cleansing, screening re-tune on Siron/FICO, managed services).
signals.likelihood: High that remediation is under-scoped in UA banks
signals.followup: Check NBU's ISO20022 document library (bank.gov.ua/files/ISO20022/) for any 2026 clarification on address structure for cross-border; the SEP ISO 20022 landing page returned 404 this run.

signals.entity: TIPS Clone (Banca d'Italia) - Western Balkans central banks
signals.country: Bosnia & Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia
signals.signal: CORRECTION TO BASELINE. Banca d'Italia's announcement (20/07/2026) records that the TIPS Clone instant-payment settlement platform went live on 20/07/2026 with a FIRST WAVE of TWO central banks - the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina AND the Central Bank of Montenegro (the baseline recorded BiH only). A second onboarding window is scheduled for NOVEMBER 2026, when the Central Bank of Albania, the Central Bank of Kosovo and the National Bank of North Macedonia are expected to join, bringing all participating countries onto the platform. The announcement states TIPS Clone 'uses the same technology as TIPS' but operates as a standalone, independent system; it does not state ISO 20022 message specifications explicitly.
signals.source_name: Banca d'Italia, 'TIPS Clone platform for instant payments in the Western Balkans goes live'
signals.implies: TIPS technology means TIPS message specs, i.e. ISO 20022 pacs.008/pacs.002 on the SCT Inst model - so the November 2026 wave forces AL/XK/MK commercial banks onto ISO 20022 instant rails in the same month as the CBPR+/EPC address break. Named Printec reference customers OTP Albania and Raiffeisen Albania sit directly in this wave. The banks must buy: instant-payment message adaptors, 24/7 real-time sanctions screening (SCT Inst requires screening within seconds - Siron/FICO), 24/7 transaction monitoring (INETCO) and 24/7 managed operations. Budget must already be committed; anything not committed by ~Sep-2026 will slip to a 2027 remediation.
signals.likelihood: High - firm month named by the operator
signals.followup: Get the exact November 2026 date and the commercial-bank participant list per country from BoA, CBK and NBRNM. Baseline noted only three BiH banks (Intesa, Raiffeisen, Sparkasse) connected domestically - re-check.

signals.signal: VERIFIED GAP. The Czech National Bank's official CERTIS description page contains ZERO references to ISO 20022 (checked by full-text scan of cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/certis/popis-systemu-certis/ this run): CERTIS, the sole CZK interbank system, has no published ISO 20022 migration and therefore no November 2026 address obligation. Czech PSPs' ISO 20022 obligation arrives instead through Reg (EU) 2024/886: ability to RECEIVE instant euro credit transfers from 09/01/2027 and to SEND plus provide Verification of Payee from 09/07/2027 - both of which are SCT Inst, i.e. EPC-rulebook, i.e. subject to the 15/11/2026 structured/hybrid address rule from day one.
signals.source_name: Czech National Bank, 'Popis systemu CERTIS' (official system description)
signals.implies: Sequencing insight that applies equally to CZ, HU and RO: any PSP building euro SCT Inst capability for the 09/01/2027 receive deadline must build it structured/hybrid-address-native, because the unstructured format expires 15/11/2026 - BEFORE their instant go-live. Building to the old format is pure rework. Budget-commit window for the Jan-2027 receive obligation: now through roughly October 2026. Affected CZ banks: Ceska sporitelna, CSOB, Komercni banka, Moneta, Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit CZ, Air Bank, Fio.
signals.likelihood: Certain (regulation) / High (CERTIS stays out of scope)
signals.followup: Watch for any CNB CERTIS ISO 20022 announcement; none exists as at 27/08/2026. Same check needed for NBS-SK and Bankart/Banka Slovenije (not reached this run).

signals.entity: CPMI / BIS - guidance for non-EU footprint central banks
signals.country: Footprint-wide (esp. BA, RS, ME, MK, AL, XK, UA)
signals.signal: CPMI Brief No 11, 'The future of financial messaging: navigating the ISO 20022 migration journey' (BIS, April 2026), sets out the migration journey in pre-migration / migration / post-migration phases and restates the CPMI harmonisation requirements, including HR9 (structured agent identifiers - BIC), HR10 (structured person identification) and HR11 'To provide a common minimum level of postal address information'. It draws on the experience of the 60+ central banks in the CoPS community and is explicitly aimed at operators still planning a migration.
signals.source_name: Bank for International Settlements / CPMI, Brief No 11 (Cornejo, Fahrmann, Kanaguchi, Lammer, Mulaudzi, Orina, Semorile)
signals.implies: This is the document CBBH, NBS Serbia, CBCG, NBRNM, CBK and BoA will be judged against by the ECB/EU accession process and by their correspondent banks. It gives Printec a credible, non-vendor framing for readiness assessments in the non-euro Balkans - the phase language ('pre-migration', 'stakeholder engagement') maps directly to a scoped assessment engagement ahead of any national cutover. NOTE: it names no countries and sets no dates, so it cannot be cited as evidence of any national deadline.
signals.followup: Use as the anchor for a Western Balkans ISO 20022 readiness offer ahead of the TIPS Clone November 2026 wave and the CBBH RTGS MX notice.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no checkpoint existed for 27/08/2026). Primary-source-first sweep of the ISO 20022 workstream across the 17-country footprint, in English plus Hungarian, Croatian, Bosnian/Serbian (Latin and Cyrillic), Bulgarian, Romanian, Czech, Slovene, Ukrainian and Greek. OPENED AND READ AT PRIMARY LEVEL: EPC153-22 v2.1 full PDF (address rules s6.1-6.4 verified verbatim); Bundesbank T2 R2026.NOV release deck 30/04/2026 (PDF text extracted locally); ECB change request T2-0170-SYS PDF (the ISO MR2019 RTGS carve-out - a material correction nobody in the baseline had); Sluzbeni glasnik BiH 09/26 of 06/02/2026 via CBBH (RTGS MT/MX decision, verbatim); CBBH Ziro kliring page and 2019 press release; BNB TARGET-BNB page with the full 19-bank participant list and the 15/06/2026 rules date; MNB business-terms annex index (to 03/08/2026) and Annex 2 of 27/10/2025 (VIBER pacs.008/009 confirmed); MNB VIBER page; CNB CERTIS description page (full-text scanned, zero ISO 20022 hits); NBU SEP page; sepa.hr Croatian SEPA Forum news; Banca d'Italia TIPS Clone announcement; BIS CPMI Brief No 11 (April 2026, PDF). GENUINE GAPS, stated honestly: (1) BNR ReGIS and TARGET-Romania - bnr.ro serves menu-only HTML to non-JS clients, the 2153/2155 deep links returned navigation chrome only, so I could NOT verify Romania's RTGS address position this run and have NOT carried the baseline's CPMI ReGIS claim forward as fact; (2) Greece, Cyprus, Slovakia, Slovenia and Austria - no national ISO 20022 address publication reached; all five are euro-area and ride T2 plus the EPC rulebook, so the T2/EPC rows cover them, but no BoG, CBC, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije/Bankart or OeNB primary page was opened; (3) Serbia - the NBS site returned 404 on every payment-system path I tried (nbs.rs/sr and /en variants) and the WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I could locate the two May-2026 Governor's acts on MT/MX coexistence named in the baseline, so the Serbian coexistence position is NOT re-verified this run and is deliberately NOT reported as a signal; (4) Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Albania national positions are covered only indirectly via the TIPS Clone row. VERIFICATION DEBTS CLOSED: Hungary's VIBER hybrid-address gap is confirmed still open against MNB's own current annex set. DEBTS NOT IN SCOPE of this workstream (Cyprus EAA, Cyprus VoP, AT/HR EUDI, DORA subcontracting RTS, HU ATM decree, BG instant legal basis, UA banknote) were not attempted. CROSS-CUTTING JUDGEMENT for the Orchestrator: the 6-12-month budget-commit window for the 14-15/11/2026 dates has ALREADY CLOSED - as at 27/08/2026 the sellable work is remediation, reject/NAK handling, screening re-tuning and managed services, not programme delivery. The forward budget-commit windows are (a) the T2 RTGS ISO MR2025 wave in November 2027, (b) the TIPS Clone November 2026 Western Balkans onboarding, (c) the CBBH RTGS MX notice with only 15 days' warning, and (d) the CZ/HU/RO euro-instant obligations of 09/01/2027 and 09/07/2027.
